additional_info.subject: Re: 0425510-DC/Si-D/FR-[ Y2 / PD 312571675/24] Temperature Sensor Fault CRM:02888000001
additional_info.body:
Hello team,
Greetings of the day!
As per the customer-
The fans are running at a high speed even though no charging has taken place. The ambient temperature is not high (16 degrees).
We have checked in logs and found that- the temperature inside the charger is also normal.
Refer logs below:
2025-05-20T12:15:58.890144+00:00 [FW060103G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4127] [TLG] |Tstamp=1747743301|Mains-P=INVAL|DC1-P=0|DC2-P=0|DC3-P=0|DC4-P=0|Ovheat=0|Mfan=0|Afan=0|EB1=0|BT1-T=25.5|BT2-T=22.4|BT3-T=21.8|BT4-T=19.8|BT5-T=19.4|MFan-T=INVAL|BT1-H=39|BT2-H=46|
Also when we checked through the debug station, we found that FAN is in off condition.
Hence, we suspect some issue with the FAN. To confirm the same, we need to check following connections:
When there is no charging/heater is OFF- there should be 0V on terminal highlighted above diagram
When there is charging session/heater is ON- the voltage should vary from 0-10 V as per the diagram.
Also attaching KA just for your reference:
Knowledge Article: Knowledge Article for ISP: Emobility_SID_HW_BT5_MainFanGQ1_XD9.2B - Dynamics 365
Knowledge Article: Knowledge Article for ISP: Emobility_SICD_HW_Mainfan_GQ1_Ok Signal Lost-Fan rotation disabled - Dynamics 365
If all the above connections and commands (0-10v) found to be OK, then remove the wires from “XD7.1B - 6,7" and check the voltage across (0-10V and GND).
NOTE: If voltage across GND and 0-10v found to be 0V, but still FAN is running at high speed then FAN needs to be replaced.
MLFB for the FAN is attached below, in case if replacement is required:
Do let us know if you have any other queries?
Thank you
Best Regards
eMobility Tech Support Team - Vaishnavi Raut
